description_full: Cmb.Tech NV engages in marine transportation business in Belgium. It operates through three divisions: Marine, H2 Infra, and H2 Industry. The Marine division designs, builds, owns, and operates various low and zero carbon ships and vessels, such as crew transfer vessels, ferries, commissioning service operations vessels, tugboats, ammonia-powered large bulk carriers, container ships, and chemical and crude oil tankers. The H2 Infra division develops and secures green molecule supplies; and produces and distributes green hydrogen and ammonia. The H2 Industry division provides scalable dual-fuel industrial applications. The company was formerly known as Euronav NV and changed its name to Cmb.Tech NV in October 2024. Cmb.Tech NV was founded in 1989 and is headquartered in Antwerp, Belgium. Cmb.Tech NV is a subsidiary of CMB NV.

financial_summary: CMB.TECH NV is a mid-cap energy business with a $5.1B market cap on $940M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +31% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 17% against a 10% cost of capital, a 7-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it.
Accruals are elevated at +10.5% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.2× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 5.9×.

Management returns a meaningful 21.9% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 57% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 9.8× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
